title: Mind–Models–World
content_html:
Mind–Models–World

Layer A — Self‑Sufficiency Loop Only (Mind ↔ Models)

Internally coherent frameworks can be generated and sustained by the mind without direct constraint from the world.

Layer B — Empirical Feedback Loop Only (Models ↔ World)

Models gain traction through predictive success and correction from observation, experiment, and measurement.

Layer C — Combined View

Self-sufficiency loop (dashed): the mind can generate frameworks (physics, metaphysics) that are coherent on their own, even without direct reference to external reality. These systems can be self-sustaining, like mathematics.

Empirical feedback loop (solid): models succeed or fail based on how well they track regularities in the world. Physics gains power not only from internal coherence but also from predictive accuracy when tested against observations.

This dual structure reflects why physics and metaphysics can feel both self-contained and yet constrained by reality: they are simultaneously creations of the mind and adaptive interfaces with the world. Both loops operate together in science and philosophy; models are at once conceptually generated and empirically constrained.

Notes & Implications

  • Constructivist insight: Categories and models are mind-made; coherence can be achieved independently of reality-testing.
  • Realist constraint: Predictive success suggests our models track some structure of the world (structural realism).
  • Interface view: Models function as interfaces translating between mind and world; accuracy is graded, not absolute.
